facts.text: Casa Grande began in 1879 as a railroad stop called Terminus, the temporary end of the Southern Pacific line.
In 1880 the settlement was renamed Casa Grande after the nearby Casa Grande Ruins National Monument, a Hohokam structure built around 1350.
The city’s roots trace back to the ancient Hohokam people, whose sophisticated irrigation ruins still dot the landscape.
When the mining boom faded in the 1890s, agriculture saved Casa Grande, keeping the town alive until it incorporated in 1915.
The Casa Grande Cotton Kings, founded in 1948, won ten straight National Baseball Congress World Series appearances by winning state titles in the 1940s and 1950s.
Today Lucid Motors and Abbott Nutrition are among the city’s largest employers, reflecting Casa Grande’s shift toward high‑tech industry.
